root_cause.text: The i.MX remoteproc implementation in `imx_rproc_elf_find_loaded_rsc_table()` incorrectly treated the device-tree `priv->rsc_table` pointer as proof of a loaded firmware resource table, without checking `rproc->table_ptr`, so firmware images lacking an actual resource table were misreported as valid and triggered a crash in remoteproc core handling.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (!rproc->table_ptr) return NULL;` before returning `priv->rsc_table`, and the CVE description says the function “still returns `priv->rsc_table`, and the remoteproc core interprets this as a valid loaded resource table” even when “the current firmware has no resource table” and `rproc->table_ptr is NULL`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Return no resource table when the firmware does not provide one.
intent_record.what: Inserted an early NULL check in `imx_rproc_elf_find_loaded_rsc_table()`: if `rproc->table_ptr` is not set, the function now returns `NULL` immediately before checking `priv->rsc_table`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now treats firmware without a resource table as having no loaded resource table and avoids proceeding with the existing lookup path. This prevents later code from assuming a resource table exists when `rproc->table_ptr` is absent.

grouping_result.intent: Return no resource table when the firmware does not provide one.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the bug: it prevents reporting a resource table when the firmware does not actually provide one, which is the missing validation that caused the i.MX remoteproc crash.

candidates.rationale: This condition treats the platform-provided resource-table pointer as sufficient evidence that a firmware resource table exists, which is the root mistake. It ignores whether the firmware actually loaded a table (rproc->table_ptr), allowing images without a real resource table to be misreported as valid.

This return hands back the device-tree resource-table pointer directly, causing remoteproc to believe a resource table is present even when the firmware did not provide one. That false positive is what leads to the crash in core handling.

vuln_statements.explanation: This condition incorrectly treats the platform/device-tree resource-table pointer as proof that a firmware resource table was actually loaded, without checking the firmware-backed table pointer. That false positive is the root cause of the crash.
This statement returns the device-tree resource-table pointer directly, causing remoteproc core to believe a valid firmware resource table exists even when the firmware image provided none.
